newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Amoco to cut staff in Russian oil projects.
newsitem.headline: Amoco to cut staff in Russian oil projects.

text.p: Amoco Corp of the United States said on Tuesday it would cut staff on its multi-billion dollar Russian oil projects due to Moscow's slow progress in passing adequate tax and natural resource laws.

Dan Westbrook, senior vice-president and resident manager of Amoco unit Amoco Eurasia Petroleum Company, told a news conference that "a slower than anticipated pace in the development of legislative and tax issues" was behind the cuts.
He did not say how many staff were affected, but stressed they were all Moscow-based.
He said the company, part of two large production-sharing projects, remained committed to doing business in Russia.
"We have not dropped any of our Russia projects," Westbrook said, adding that Amoco was pursuing deals and aimed to give the Russian side a 50 percent stake in each of them.

Russia has a production-sharing law but has not yet amended it to mesh with other legislation or smoothed out tax issues. It has not yet passed a list detailing which reserves are open to production-sharing.
Amoco is negotiating with YUKOS on the Priobsk field and has a 20 percent stake in the international Timan-Pechora Company, which is also eyeing northern reserves.

In a third project, Amoco representatives met officials from Rosneft, the state oil holding company that is being privatised, and exploration outfit Arkhangelskgeoldobycha to talk about setting up a consortium to tap reserves in the Khoreiverskaya Basin in oil rich Timan-Pechora in the Far North.

The three companies bid jointly in a tender for the reserves, but Russian officials declared every company which bid, including other Western ones, winners and asked them to form a consortium. Rosneft spokesman Vladimir Tumarkin said a consortium could be announced by November 25.
All three projects are in a region with no infrastructure, making them dependent on each other for pipelines planned to export production.
"All the projects in the area are co-dependent, if you will," Amoco Eurasia Petroleum Company vice-president William Thomas told the same news conference.
"There are only a few companies in the world that are going to be able to develop these reserves and have the Arctic expertise."
